bib.title: ReST meets ReAct: Self-Improvement for Multi-Step Reasoning LLM Agent

question: Can a ReAct-style multi-step search agent be improved, and distilled into much smaller models, by iterative fine-tuning on its own trajectories using only AI feedback and no human labels?
hypothesis: A ReST-like grow/improve loop with LLM-based ranking of per-step samples can improve a process-based agent and transfer to smaller models.
contributions: A flavor of ReAct agent with self-critique for long-form question answering
A proxy evaluation metric based on Bamboogle and BamTwoogle with emphasis on auto-eval
ReST-style iterative fine-tuning on the agent's reasoning traces improves the agent
Improvement from stepwise AI feedback only, no human-labeled training data
Synthetic data distils the agent into one or two orders of magnitude smaller models with comparable performance

method.summary: A five-step Search Agent state machine (decide, search, summarize, answer, relevance and grounding self-checks) is prompted as Python code on PaLM 2-L. Trajectories from 2000 questions are split into per-step examples, best samples chosen by perplexity or an LLM ranker, and PaLM 2 XS/S/L are fully fine-tuned on them. The process repeats with the fine-tuned L to give a 2nd generation, and small models are trained on the same data (self-distillation).
method.task: long-form, attributable question answering with web search as a tool; evaluated on multi-hop compositional QA

other.uses: prompted teacher, fine-tuned agent, auto-eval judge (base), ranker (instruction-tuned)

other.note: abstract claims two orders of magnitude fewer parameters than L; no parameter counts given

training.objective: full fine-tuning on per-reasoning-step examples from completed trajectories (next-token on step outputs, inferred)

other.checkpoints_chosen: step 9K for XS, 5K for S, 3.5K for L (chosen by Bamboogle auto-eval)
other.mixture_sizes: pilot 500 trajectories; 1st gen 2000 trajectories (17970 examples); 2nd gen 8000 trajectories = 2000 questions x4 (72424 examples), 1x 18007, 2x 36238
other.iteration: 1st gen from prompted PaLM 2-L; 2nd gen trajectories from PaLM 2-L fine-tuned on 1st gen; each size fine-tuned on each mixture
other.fine_tune_from: inferred: each model fine-tuned from its pre-trained checkpoint on each mixture (text says 'fine-tune the new model (of the same size)')
other.ranking: instruction-tuned PaLM 2-L ranks 4 sampled outputs per step (0-shot, Listing 8); used off-policy for fine-tuning data; on-policy rollouts use min perplexity; one iteration of 'improve'

inference.decoding: sampling; per step choose lowest-perplexity sample
inference.samples: per reasoning step: 4 samples for L and S, 16 for XS; evaluation over 10 trajectories per Bamboogle question
inference.prompting: few-shot prompts formatted as Python code, per step: decision 9-shot, summarization 6-shot, answer generation 5-shot, relevance self-check 6-shot, grounding self-check 5-shot, auto-eval 5-shot, reward model 0-shot
inference.retrieval: internal Google Q&A API, top-3 snippets per query, at most 10 searches per trajectory (REMAINING SEARCHES field)

parameters.state: PAST_ACTIONS field stores all actions so far

metrics.name: Bamboogle auto-eval accuracy
metrics.definition: separate PaLM 2-L base call (5-shot prompt) checks whether the final answer implies the reference answer; mean and std over 10 runs

metrics.name: Human accuracy
metrics.definition: manual correctness judgement of a single run

baselines: Pilot data (human filtered / unfiltered) fine-tuned models
eval.protocol: auto-eval validated against human ratings (Pearson 0.98, Spearman 0.83); BamTwoogle held out as test; human eval single run; no significance tests beyond std

availability.data: BamTwoogle not stated as released; prompts in Appendix Listings 1-8

prompts.purpose: Reward model ranking of 4 sampled outputs
prompts.text:
Rater Instructions:
- The goal of this rating is to filter out bad actions, so that they’ll be excluded from the fine-tuning dataset.
- Overall, we want to the agent to produce relevant and grounded answers with minimal steps. Anything that deviates from this goal is considered bad.
- If any element (thoughts, comments etc.) is empty, then it’s automatically bad.

limits: Authors concede: manually constructed prompts, small evals, a limited set of models, and only a single tool.
Only two self-improvement iterations; saturation point unknown.
Whether the loop works with multiple tools or unseen tools is untested.
Bamboogle and BamTwoogle are small (125 and 100 questions); human evals are single runs.
No learning rate, optimizer, batch size, hardware or compute reported; PaLM 2 sizes and the search API are not public, so not reproducible.
Teacher-capped: small models are distilled from prompted L data; whether they exceed it is left open.
Auto-eval is run by PaLM 2-L; number of agents behind the 0.98 correlation is not stated.
